links.outcome: Radiologist AUC across AI interface designs versus no AI
links.effect: Text-only improved AUC vs no AI (0.87 vs 0.82; P < .001); text plus confidence score (0.77 vs 0.82; P = .46) and text, score, and overlay (0.80 vs 0.82; P = .66) showed no improvement.
links.quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve improved when radiologists used the text-only output compared with no AI (0.87 vs 0.82; P < .001).

links.outcome: Radiologist performance with versus without AI in intended deployment mode
links.effect: Performance depended on interface; text-only improved AUC 0.82 to 0.87 (P < .001), other interfaces showed no difference vs no AI.
links.quote: There was no difference in performance for the combined text and AI confidence score output compared with no AI (0.77 vs 0.82; P = .46) and for the combined text, AI confidence score, and image overlay output compared with no AI (0.80 vs 0.82; P = .66).

links.outcome: Reader performance with AI in different interface configurations versus no AI
links.effect: Text-only UI AUC 0.87 vs 0.82 without AI (P < .001); other UIs no significant difference; 8 of 10 preferred the overlay UI despite no performance gain.
links.quote: Text-only UI output significantly improved radiologist performance compared with no AI in the detection of lung nodules and masses on chest radiographs, but user preference did not correspond with user performance.

links.outcome: Effect of output presentation formats (text, score, image overlay) on reader AUC
links.effect: Richer output (score, overlay) did not improve performance versus no AI (0.77 and 0.80 vs 0.82), while text-only did (0.87); 80% preferred the overlay output.
links.quote: Eight of the 10 radiologists (80%) preferred the combined text, AI confidence score, and image overlay output over the other two interfaces.

unlisted_practices: Do not rely on user preference to choose AI interface design; test interface impact on performance
